subtopicTitle: Payload fraction as function of Δv and Isp

cards.front: Define payload fraction for a rocket.
cards.back: Payload fraction $\eta$ is the ratio of payload mass $m_{pl}$ to initial mass $m_0$: $\eta = m_{pl}/m_0$.

cards.front: State the ideal rocket equation relating $\Delta v$, $I_{sp}$, and mass ratio.
cards.back: $\Delta v = I_{sp} g_0 \ln(m_0/m_f)$ or equivalently $m_0/m_f = \exp(\Delta v/(I_{sp} g_0))$, where $v_e = I_{sp} g_0$.

cards.front: Derive ideal payload fraction (zero structural mass) as function of $\Delta v$ and $I_{sp}$.
How does ideal payload fraction change if $\Delta v$ doubles (fixed $I_{sp}$)?
cards.back: $\eta$ is squared: new $\eta' = [\exp(-\Delta v/(I_{sp} g_0))]^2$. Payload fraction drops exponentially with $\Delta v$.

cards.front: How does ideal payload fraction change if $I_{sp}$ doubles (fixed $\Delta v$)?
cards.back: Exponent halved: $\eta' = \exp(-\Delta v/(2 I_{sp} g_0))$, so payload fraction increases (closer to 1).

cards.front: Write payload fraction when a constant structural factor $\epsilon = m_{struct}/m_p$ is included.
What happens to payload fraction as $\Delta v \to 0$ or $I_{sp} \to \infty$?
cards.back: As $\Delta v \to 0$ or $I_{sp} \to \infty$, $\eta 	o 1$ (all initial mass can be payload).

cards.front: Why real payload fraction is always lower than the ideal $\exp(-\Delta v/v_e)$ expression.
cards.back: Non-zero structural mass $m_{struct}>0$ reduces usable payload: $m_{pl} = m_f - m_{struct}$, so $\eta < \exp(-\Delta v/v_e)$.
